utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this Courtroom number III. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. There seem to be no preliminaries. Ms. Marcus, are you ready to continue your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then before we continue, I'd like to again, Mr. Karan, remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Karan.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please call up P235, the first page for now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, a log-book of entries from the Pauk headquarters has been admitted into evidence in this case. This is an operational log-book containing hour-by-hour and sometimes minute-by-minute operational activities regarding combat operations carried out by the Joint Command in Operation Pauk. Did you ever have the opportunity to see this log-book during your visits to Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not see that. The first time I've ever seen it was here when I arrived in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I please have page 9 in English, which corresponds to page 15 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Karan, this log-book contains entries describing, as I said, hour to hour combat activities, including the activities of Milorad Ulemek, aka Legija, and Raja Bozovic, both of who you agree commanded tactical groups in Velika Kladusa in the Pauk operation. For your information, there are 47 mentions of Bozovic and 78 mentions of Legija in this operational log-book. What you see in front of you is an example of one of the pages from the log-book. These entries are from the 17th of November, 1994. Let me give you just a moment to have a look at it. Could I draw your attention to the middle of the page to the entry at 1005. It says: "Observe targets, you will get fire." And you can see the entry to Bozovic to the right of that. At 1040 it says: "Atalusa to be fired on by tanks, BOV-3." At 1120, you can see helicopters landed near Cazin from the correction of Plitvice, Muslims have abandoned Ripac and still hold half of Grabez. And to the right of that, you see the entry Frenki and RPG. A bit further down you will see at 1320 an entry which says: "Muslims are organising a counter-attack from the direction of Vrnograc," and to the right of that you see again RPG and Frenki. Do you know who bore the nickname RPG?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never -- RPG [Realtime transcript read in error "APG"] is the abbreviation for the radio interception group or, rather, the centre that was on Petrova Gora.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So based on what you have told us about Frenki's activities in the context of the Pauk operation in terms of gathering reconnaissance, isn't it a fact that these entries describe combat operations, not purely reconnaissance activities?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Let's comment upon the entry at 1120 where it says: "Three helicopters landed near Cazin from the direction of Plitvice." You could observe that from the ground as well. However, when it comes to electronic surveillance, electronic surveillance is the best to observe such activities and at the same time Muslims are organising a counter attack from the direction of Vrgorac which means that they were listening into the communications of the 5th Corps. So it is easy to conclude that this is, in practical term, an intelligence activity and not a combat activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for interjecting, but I would like to say that on line 7 the abbreviation is misrecorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It should be RPG. That's hereby corrected. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the Court Officer please call up 65 ter 6402. Your Honours, this is a demonstrative exhibit which the Prosecution has prepared. It contains excerpts of P235. There is nothing in here which is not in P235. It's merely a copy in place of excerpts and we only need to show one because the document has both B/C/S and English on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, the log-book, the Pauk operational log-book which I've been showing you contains 15 entries discussing the activities of Frenki, Franko Simatovic, as part of the Pauk operations. I have taken some of them and put them on this exhibit. Could you have a look at some of the entries on this page which are from the Pauk log-book, and then I will ask you a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you want the witness to look at some of them or all of them?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: All of them, please, sir. Could you tell me when you're finished with page 1.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm done. I'm done.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could we have page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Done.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Isn't it a fact, Mr. Karan, that these entries describe Frenki's involvement in the planning and carrying out of combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I'm reading this, I can say that he was partly involved in combat operation activities. However, I don't see his direct command over the entire thing. This is more of informative nature, i.e., one can see that he arrived for the briefings and briefings, and it was up to the person who entered all those entries in the log-book how he did it. I didn't see him there. I didn't go there that often, so I can't claim for a fact whether he was the one who was in charge of combat operations or not. As far as I know, electronic surveillance is a very complex activity, so if he could and if he was able to command combat activities and combat operations, then I would say "chapeau" to him. And I don't know what General Novakovic would have been doing in that case. He was the commander. He was an experienced officer as well as Colonel Bulat, who was a lecturer at the high military school. He was well-versed in -- on combat operations. I really don't know how much Frenki knew about conducting combat operations. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: On the 23rd of February, at page 17716, you were asked: "Did you know what duties Mr. Simatovic discharged at that time?" This was in connection to Pauk. Your answer was: "I knew that he had gathered a group of engineers and technicians that were involved in electronic surveillance. He headed that group. He co-ordinated their work, and that's all I knew and all I needed to know, for that matter." Coming from a security operative, your comment surprised me. In fact, on the 23rd of February, at page 17686, you stated: "I emphasised yesterday that I can only speak about the security situation in my unit, and in that sense I can also talk competently about the security situation in the area of that unit, that is Western Bosnia and the area bordering Croatia." Wasn't it then centrally within your responsibilities to know as much as you can about the situation in your area?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that I said that I -- that my responsibility was the territory of Western Bosnia. Actually, I am now claiming that I never said that. This may have been misinterpreted. I absolutely claim that in my area of responsibility, the area of responsibility of the 21st Corps, I was really responsible for the security situation. Yes, the command of Operation Pauk was within my area of responsibility, but it was not under the command of the 21st Corps but under the command of the Main Staff. I did not have any operational needs to monitor the activities and actions of the Pauk operation command because they were not our enemy, and that was the simple reason. And it is true that I said that Mr. Simatovic worked on Petrova Gora and that he was involved in electronic surveillance together with a team of people. As I've already told you, this is a very complex activity, and to this very day I still claim that it would be practically impossible to do both things at the same time, because it doesn't suffice only to intercept conversations. These conversations have to be analysed and -- and then translated into valuable reports to be sent to those that they were intended for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, you said you don't remember that you said that your responsibility was the territory of Western Bosnia, and does that include what Ms. Marcus read, Western Bosnia and the area bordering Croatia? You said you don't remember that. And then you continued by saying you even claim that you did not say it and that it might be misinterpreted. Now, it's relatively easy for us to verify whether you said that or not. If it is your claim that your words were not -- that's not what you said and that it may have been wrongly translated, we'll verify that. Is that -- is your claim so strong as -- that we should verify it, because we do not wish to misunderstand your testimony. So if you say you still claim this is not what you said, we'll have it verified and then it's all audio recorded, both your words and the interpretation, so if you say, My claim stands, then we'll do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stick by my claim. I was in no position to ever say that my responsibility was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether you were in a position or not, the question is whether you did say it or whether you didn't say it, and it will be verified on the basis of the audio recording of both your words and the translation and what is transcribed. Ms. Marcus, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karan, wouldn't it have been part of your responsibility to at least be aware who was operating in the -- in your area of responsibility, what their activities involved, for security reasons at least but also for information-sharing purposes toward a common goal?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're right, yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In fact, twice you used a possessive term when you were speaking about the police both on your testimony at 23rd of February. The first time was at page 17692 where you said: "I know that we provided Fikret Abdic with police escorts." And the second time at page 17702 where you said: "My police intervened in such incidents." It seems you did view the police activities, at least as falling into your purview, certainly your knowledge, in fact, it appears from your comments your -- your direct involvement, but with respect to a high-level Serbian MUP official such as Franko Simatovic, you did not need to know more about what he was doing other than co-ordinating the work of a group of engineers and technicians in electronic surveillance?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what your question is. If I was talking about my military -- my police, maybe I didn't explain myself fully. It was the military police, and I was responsible for them in professional terms, and maybe it is my mistake that I used the possessive "mine." We did provide some of the support in addition to the civilian police to Fikret Abdic, and I was responsible for issuing permits for movement to members of the armed forces in the Western Bosnia region. I was the one who was exclusively responsible to issue them permits for their unhindered movement in order to be able to carry out their activities in gathering units together, preparing for combat operations and similar things.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I please have page 1 again. Back to page 1. Mr. Karan, today, just before at pages 4 and 5, when I asked you about Frenki's involvement in planning and carrying out of combat operations, part your answer was: "I can say that he was partly involved in combat operation activities. However, I don't see his direct command over the entire thing. This is more of informative nature. One can see that he arrived for the briefings, and it was up to the person who entered those entries how he did it. I didn't see him there. I didn't go there that often, so I can't claim for a fact whether he was the one who was in charge of combat operations or not." And you continue to explain how difficult and complex electronic surveillance is. In fact, wouldn't it be consistent with the role of security operatives to gathering intelligence and reconnaissance and use that in guiding combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean me or Mr. Simatovic? Who do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Well, I would -- I think it applies to both, but let's answer about Mr. Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Simatovic could collect intelligence by electronic surveillance. I did not have such means. I didn't do that. I'm not an intelligence officer, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: My question to you is: Isn't it consistent, isn't it possible that he could have been gathering intelligence and reconnaissance and using that in the planning of combat operations? Isn't that the entire purpose of gathering intelligence and reconnaissance in the context of war?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, I -- I'm not sure that the question is as clear as it could be, because it's not totally clear to me, or at least it's not clear to me. It's not clear to me whether my learned friend is suggesting that the security officer gathers the information and then personally uses it to -- for combat or gathers the information and then gives it to another to be used in combat? I think that might be the confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, there is some merit in this observation, I think. I mean, the use of intelligence and reconnaissance in combat, even if that would be the purpose and the aim of gathering it, then that doesn't say that much about how it is used, by whom it is used, whether it's passed on, or whether that means that the person gathering that is -- is using it himself for the follow-up or the simultaneous combat operations. So there is some ambiguity in that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I was hoping the witness could shed some light on the relationship between gathering reconnaissance and combat activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but then you should put your questions in such a way that there's no ambiguity in it because the risk of getting more confused is greater than that we better understand it. Apart from that, the witness said what he knew and what he doesn't know, and of course this is a question which is rather on the theoretical level, whether this is the aim and whether it could be understood as whether the witness seems to have no direct knowledge of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, respectfully, I do think that he does have knowledge. He was a security officer and engaged in combat operations, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but when he asked, Are you talking about me or about Mr. Simatovic, then you said, Let's focus on Mr. Simatovic. So if you want to put the same question to him in relation to himself, then of course that's a different question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. I will do that in a few moments, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- with the -- in the back of your mind the observations made. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, let me try this again. With respect to Mr. Simatovic, would it necessarily be inconsistent to say that Mr. Simatovic may have been gathering reconnaissance, gathering intelligence, and also used that information in the planning and carrying out of combat operations, based on your experience?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying again it was practically impossible physically to do both, because anyone involved in gathering intelligence through electronic surveillance knows what demanding work it is, and it would take a super man to plan combat activities at the same time to the extent I've done the same things within my service. I know this, because what would be the purpose of that? If he did it, then the Pauk command was not necessary, nor was it necessary to attach part of the corps command. The general would not have been needed at the head of it all. The Chief of Staff who was in the rank of colonel or general would not need to be attached to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, I hear your reasoning and you were speculation. Let me ask you specifically about your knowledge. Let's look at the first page of the -- that's in front of us. The first entry on the 18th of November 1994: "Frenki requests that Alatusa and Plazikur be the first targets. Do the job with 82-millimetre mortars. Do the job with our co-ordination. What I am sending I will send to Ramici. When you get to Atalusa open fire on Plazikur." Let's move to the next one, same day a little bit later: "Frenki is looking for Bozovic to insert our forces (MUP)." Next entry: "Frenki is sending four Maljutkas operators and two suitcases to Kole in Katinovac." Now, these entries, Mr. Karan, do describe, as you said earlier, Frenki being involved, at least in planning, and arguably with the first one even co-ordinating combat operations; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what is written here you could say that's true. However, he's the first one to learn the movements of the enemy, and he's the first one in a position to react, because you can see here that he is informing someone.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That is precisely my point, Mr. Karan. Frenki was in a position to obtain this information and use that information in the planning of combat operations. Isn't -- did I understand your evidence correctly?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, because the person who first learns about the movements of the 5th Corps, or whichever other enemy, must pass on that information to the units that are involved, that are fighting that enemy. You can see -- or you can't see from this that he is involved in the co-ordination of any activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this demonstrative exhibit. It's 65 ter 6402.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry. Could I just inquire whether this has been in another form exhibited before. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Ms. Marcus told us it's an extract from a log-book.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Yes, these are excerpts from -- just simply cut and paste excerpts from the log-book admitted as P235.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6402 will receive number P3091, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3091 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please call up P3024.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What you see in front of you is a document which is in evidence in this case. It is a report from the Serbian DB JATD dated February 1995 several months after we say the Serbian DB became directly involved in the Pauk Joint Command. On the first page you can see an overview of command post security. May I please have page 2 in both languages. On page 2 you see descriptions of convoy escorts and laying an ambush. It says under "laying an ambush": "The following members participated in the ambush: "Keres," that is, by the way, Janko Keres, the author of the document, "Jankovic, Dukic, Kuburovic, two Z-M Strela shoulder-launched rocket system operators from the ARSK and two communications operators ..." Could I please have page 3 in both languages. Here on page 3 you find an entry describing the conduct of sniper operations. Near the bottom it says: "Keres, Jankovic, Suvara, Dukic, and Davidovic took part in the action." Our position, Mr. Karan, is that this report describes the co-ordinated joint combat operations in which the JATD participated with the SVK during Operation Pauk. Would you like to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, when the group for electronic surveillance arrived, and that was in about 20 vehicles carrying equipment, there arrived also 40 to 50 persons who secured that convoy and who were engaged up there in providing security to the facility at Petrova Gora itself. From this document, one could say that some of those persons who had arrived took part in the activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Combat activities you mean?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I please have page 5 in B/C/S and in English page 4. Mr. Karan, you told us earlier that you knew Rajo Bozovic and Legija to be commanders of two of the tactical groups which operated in Pauk. As you can see according to this Serbian DB report, Bozovic and Legija were issued with military equipment by the Serbian DB in November and December of 1994. Were you aware that Bozovic and Legija were operating in Operation Pauk, deployed and equipped by the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know the two of them. I only heard of them the first time when they arrived in 1994. I described to you how I addressed my superior for an explanation. I've never seen a document like this before, and I don't know that they received special equipment from the Serbian DB. I just don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Finally could I please have page 5 in English and page 6 in B/C/S. The last page of this document lists special equipment and those to whom it was issued. Do you recognise any of the names on this list?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know anyone from this list.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So you were not aware then that the individuals, these individuals, were members of the JATD of the Serbian DB during the time they were operating as part of Operation Pauk?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I believed my superior when he told me about these two, but I suppose that they had arrived with some more members of their service for security purposes, which would be normal, but I don't know any of these people.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: On the 23rd of February, at page 17707, you were asked: "Do you know that the MUP of Serbia in October 1994 or perhaps later ever sent any material and technical equipment that would be used in Operation Pauk?" And you answered: "I don't know if I was clear enough. Material and technical equipment, when it comes to counter-intelligence, are not cannons or ammunition. Those are some special-purpose equipment. So when the commander talks about MTS is one thing, and my MTS is a different thing. Our MTS is not visible, whereas the material and equipment for command and its units are lethal weapons." Would you agree with me that the equipment issued on this page and the previous page is not equipment for counter-intelligence activities, not for reconnaissance activities, but, rather, equipment directly related to armed combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I see on these lists are lights. I don't know why they would be specifically intended for combat, perhaps only movement by night. Could you perhaps show me again that previous list so I can comment, but this tells me nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I have the previous page, please, in both languages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. On this list you see that some of these are MTS for combat.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer now please call up P1285, page 4 in English and page 3 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, Mr. Bakrac showed you this document during his examination last Thursday, the 23rd of February, at page 17692. If you recall, this document dates from June 1994. It discusses the provision of weapons and ammunition to Fikret Abdic by Slobodan Milosevic through the RSK government. At page 17694, Mr. Bakrac asked you: "Sir, do you know that already in June 1994, Fikret Abdic had meetings with the President of Serbia?" And your answer was: "According to what I know, he met with the President of Serbia even before that. I know that we provided Fikret Abdic with police escorts. We even provided him with temporary force ID bearing a Serbian name so he could cross the territory of Republika Srpska on his way to Belgrade." Now, you explained to us a bit earlier that when you said police escorts, you were referring to military police escorts. What temporary force ID did you provide Abdic with?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did not understand me well. IDs were provided to Fikret Abdic for his trip to Belgrade by SUP Vojnic. We just provided escort from Velika Kladusa to Vojnic to ensure safe passage, but we were not in a position to provide documents like that because it was not within our jurisdiction, and I said earlier that I provided temporary laissez-passers to the members of the armed force of Fikret Abdic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: One of the paragraphs you were shown by Mr. Bakrac appears on the page in front of you. It begins with the words "at these meetings Abdic accepted." Could I ask you to please re-read that paragraph again to remind yourself.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm done.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: As you can see, in addition to meeting with President Milosevic, this paragraph describes Jovica Stanisic as having been present at this early planning and organisational meeting. Our position is that in addition to Slobodan Milosevic, Jovica Stanisic was also involved in the organisation of military support to Fikret Abdic and the autonomous province of Western Bosnia, and this is how command and control, in fact, worked. First there was a political decision-making process, and then as we see in the specific combat order, the military command levels use the political instruction in order to develop military plans whereby they establish specific missions for specific units.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I refer the Chamber to the transcript of 2nd November, 2010, at page 8640.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, does what I just put to you conform with your own understanding of how the support to Fikret Abdic was initially planned?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not how I would read this. You are just taking the name of Jovica Stanisic out of here, and you are omitting Momcilo Perisic. He could have also been, based on your thinking, in command of the combat operations in Western Bosnia. I believe at this meeting Jovica Stanisic is the closest associate of President Milosevic, was present because somebody from the security sector should have been present. I don't see any link between Jovica Stanisic and the command from this. Perisic could have equally been in command based on that thinking.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That's not exactly question I asked. It is clear from this that Jovica Stanisic was involved in the planning meetings, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think these meetings represented planning. Agreements were only made that something needed to be done. Planning was left to military commanders. I don't see the link, at least not from these few sentences, that he would be the only one who would be planning activities. Based on this, Perisic could have done that. What is Celeketic doing here then, or Mladic? They were certainly not just figureheads at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, I don't think the question of Ms. Marcus included that Mr. Stanisic was the only one but purely that he was involved.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand what Mrs. Marcus meant, but I cannot confirm what she wants to hear from me. Based on these five lines, I cannot give an opinion about a matter so important, although I can't rule it out either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. Please proceed, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I actually think we agree on a lot of this. What -- your answer was, though, one thing I wanted to ask about, you said: "Agreements were only made that something needs to be done. Planning was left to military commanders." The paragraph Mr. Bakrac and that I just showed you says in the first line: Abdic accepted a proposal on the offensive activities. So the agreement in this paragraph is talking about an agreement about military activities, offensive activities; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see anything controversial about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That wasn't the question, whether it's controversial. Would you please carefully listen to the question Ms. Marcus puts to you and then try to answer those questions. The question was not, Do you see anything controversial? The question was whether this agreement, what should be done, was about military activities, whether you agree with that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please call up 65 ter -- yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, I'd like to ask a follow-up question on a matter which is already a couple of minutes behind us, but perhaps the memory is still closer at this moment than if I would put the question to the witness later. Witness, you were asked by Ms. Marcus about this report, DB JATD, and she went with you through certain parts of that report. I'm talking about P3024. One of them was sniping operations conducted. You were asked about that, and Ms. Marcus wanted to know whether this report of February 1995, whether it showed a direct involvement of the Serbian DB in the joint -- in the Pauk Joint Command, and then on page 3 where the sniper operations are described, she read to you that -- some names were read to you, were -- took part in the action. Now, you responded to the question as follows, you said: "As far as I remember, when the group for electronic surveillance arrived, and that was in about 20 vehicles carrying equipment, also some 40 to 50 persons arrived who secured that convoy and who were engaged up there in providing security to the facility of Petrova Gora," and you say from this document one could say that some of those persons who had arrived took part in the activities. Now, the two activities, sniping operations are described. I'll read to you what is the second one. A member with a submachine-gun, day/night site covered a marksman with a 90-millimetre RB, and after their fire the -- after their fire, the area around the target was covered by mortar fire, and the targets were hit. Now, I do understand that this action was taken against a hotel building in which the enemy were, and then it's described how -- how this was done. Now, this description of this action, how can I reconcile that with, as you said, providing security to the facility at Petrova Gora itself? You say this can be explained by that description of -- of the duty of these 40 to 50 people. This seems to be an attack on a hotel where the enemy is lodged. Could you explain to me how should I understand this activity against this hotel or the same would be true for the two-storey building which is described as securing the facility at Petrova Gora.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not have knowledge about any activities of a certain number of persons who arrived there as a security detail. That's how they came, to provide security, and we can see from this document that there was fighting using the hand-held launcher of 19-millimetre calibre and that it was in the Cazin Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, could I then put the following to you: If an activity is described and if you say people came to provide security to the facility of Petrova Gora, would you agree with me that there are two possibilities if you see this -- this -- this operational activity described? Either you can put that activity in one way or another in the context of providing security to the facility of Petrova Gora -- that's one option. The other option is that what is described just fell out of that context, which would mean that whatever their task may have been, that they may not have performed those tasks but were engaged in activities which are foreign to their task. Would you agree that that are the two options?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on what we can see here, it is more probable that the second option that you have just laid out is true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could I request the Court Officer, please, to call up 65 ter 5608, page 188.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: My colleague Mr. Bakrac showed you this entry that you will see in a moment from the Mladic diary, dated 8th of July, 1994. This is where Mladic held a meeting attended by Milosevic, Perisic, Jovica Stanisic, Martic, Mikelic, and Djukic. The topic of conversation was what is to be done to help Fikret Abdic. Do you recall -- well, it's not up yet. When it's up, could you please tell me whether you recall having looked at that entry and then I will compare it to another one.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you recall being shown this by Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I now please request the Court Officer to call up 65 ter 5609, page 83 in both English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: This will be another entry from another part of the Mladic diaries. This is another excerpt that was shown to you by Mr. Bakrac. It was shown on the 23rd of February at page 17704. This one relates to a meeting which took place on the 4th of October, 1994. Mr. Bakrac did not tell you the participants at this meeting. In attendance were President Milosevic, General Perisic, General Celeketic, Jovica Stanisic, and General Mladic. Mr. Bakrac asked you: "Do you know something about the agreement between Milosevic, Martic, and Karadzic? What was that about?" You answered: "That was about an absolute support of Fikret Abdic in every term, especially in military terms, to help him return to the territory of Western Bosnia. That is political framework for something that the army would have to do." It seems to me in that comment that you agreed with me about the meetings establishing the political framework that set the stage for what would happen militarily. Do I have that right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you have that absolute right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with this document. Mr. Karan, isn't it a fact that in the context of war and active combat operations there are many individuals who participate in combat operations who do not stand at the front lines firing weapons and artillery?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's a fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So, for example, there are those who carry equipment, those who drive vehicles, who fly helicopters, there are those who organise logistics, and there are senior-level officers who also do not necessarily fire weapons or artillery but pass down the orders to those who do; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Similarly, there are also members who gather intelligence or reconnaissance all with the aim of protecting and ensuring the success of combat operations; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And all those individuals in the context of armed conflict are considered to have participated in combat operations, even those who didn't necessarily fire the weapons and artillery at the front lines because they all contribute to the effectiveness of the combat; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry. The question has been answered, but I would have objected to the question. It's asking the witness effectively for an opinion, but an opinion from which perspective? I mean, from a lawyer's perspective, from a witness's perspective, from an intelligence officer's perspective, from a humanitarian worker's perspective? I mean, it can be answered in so many different ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I was more thinking about asking the obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was more thinking in terms of asking for the obvious. Is it true that someone who is in charge of using a telex machine contributes to the -- of course. The one who cleans this building contributes to the success of this Tribunal, isn't it. I mean it's so obvious, Ms. Marcus. That was more my comment and it's so obvious because it's put in such general terms, and that seems to be the problem with Mr. Jordash. So both Mr. Jordash and I have some problems with this question and invite you to come to your point.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will do. Could the Court Officer please call up 65 ter 6404.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, this is a document from your military personnel file. It appears to be an assessment made of your military performance on the 8th of November, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I please request page 3 in English and page 2 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What it says here in the last line of the third paragraph is: "During combat operations, he took all measures to protect unit commands from any type of threat." That does not mean that you were at the front line firing artillery. You were consistently engaged in security-related tasks throughout the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So the mention of combat operations pertains to your work as a security operative for the military in the context of combat operations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I now please ask for 65 ter 6405.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Just would things. If my learned friend's position is that contributing intelligence to a combat operation is a contribution to a combat operation, then we agree with that. And then the second thing is would we be able to have a break, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Marcus, the first one there seems to be agreement that if that's your position, could you confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That was the position I was putting forth with this document, and then in that case I would not continue with any more questions on this but I would request that this document be admitted into evidence; that's 65 ter 6404.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I just understand the relevance and probative value of it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Well, the relevance was what we just discussed, which is that this witness's involvement in combat operations involved gathering intelligence and the role of intelligence in planning and organising and contributing that information to combat operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not know whether you are reflecting exactly what -- because the witness's involvement in combat operations involved gathering intelligence or is it that gathering intelligence would contribute and would be in support of -- could be in support of and may have been here in this document, may have been in support of combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Our position would be both, and this is only one part of that -- that argument, Your Honour. So this is one piece of it. There will be other pieces of it, of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under those circumstances, we have to look at the evidence in its totality.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, first of all, let me give the decision on admission. This -- the objection is denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, I wasn't objecting. I was just inquiring and I withdraw the objection. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So then, Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6404 will receive number P3092, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Mr. Karan, you had an objection. Do I not know yet against what, but please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An objection to the gathering of intelligence. That was not within my purview at all. I did not gather intelligence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll have an opportunity after the break, in light of the document, to further explain what you meant. We'll first take a break. Ms. Marcus, would you please take the witness back to the document and give him an opportunity after the break to comment on what he did and what he didn't do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we take a break and we resume at a quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Ms. Marcus, I would like the witness to look at a short video of part of his testimony given earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear a language which I think will be B/C/S on channel 4 which -- oh, let me see whether -- could it be I had not my -- could it be played again. And, Witness, could you please carefully listen and look at yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpret with like to know whether the portion should be interpreted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we can start without interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you have had an opportunity to look at your own testimony and hear it. Is it still your claim that you were mistranslated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not claiming that. I repeat: The autonomous region of Western Bosnia was not within my authority, but I used information that I received from that territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not asking you to comment on your testimony. Earlier, you suggested that it would be a mistranslation. You claimed that you had not said what was written in the transcript. I asked you whether you were sure your claim that what is in the transcript is not what you said. My question simply now is: Do you still claim that you have not said what was read to you as being part of the transcript? That's the only question I'd like to receive an answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not claiming that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, you shifted the blame to interpreters instead of explaining what you had intended to say but what you did not say. We took the effort to verify it after I specifically asked you whether it was still your claim that you had not said what appeared on the transcript. This Chamber, the parties know that, never accepts the interpreters to be blamed for something they should not be blamed for. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just before the break, Your Honour instructed that the within should be shown again, I see it's on the screen, that's admitted as P3092.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, you wanted to add something about this document.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to this document but to the comment that I was involved in intelligence work.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that -- I believe the witness is looking at the first page and I think he should be looking at the second page. I believe that my learned friend was showing him the second page before the break and now he has the first page before him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's correct. Could we look at the second page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no comment to what it says here. My only objection was to the Prosecutor's word to the effect that I was engaged in gathering intelligence, and that was not what I did. That was not within my purview. That was my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Would you like further clarification, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you put something to the witness and he says, That's not what I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Further clarification for us or to ask further questions to the witness, I leave it in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think what happened is that Mr. Jordash and I engaged in a discussion, and I put our position which talked about intelligence, and the witness interpreted that as what I had put to him, but, in fact, my last question to him was: "Your mention of combat operations pertains to your work as a security operative for the military in the context of combat operations." And his answer was that that was correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we can proceed, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Your Honour, before I do that, before we pass this subject and move on to another, I'd like to clarify something with the Stanisic Defence. My colleague Mr. Jordash said: "If my learned friend's position is that contributing intelligence to a combat operation is a contribution to a combat operation, then we agree with that." I'd like to understand very clearly what the Defence is agreeing to. It's the Prosecution's case that the accused, as members of a JCE, were part of the planning and direction of military operations during the indictment period. That's part of our case. Additionally, we've alleged that the accused made a significant contribution to the JCE by providing an important channel of communication between the JCE members. The Prosecution submits that the evidence in this case has shown that the intelligence collected by the DB of Serbia includes information on the upcoming movements of enemy units and formations and other related military matters. For clarity, is the Defence agreeing that the DB of Serbia collected intelligence and communicated this intelligence to military structures as part of combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think I was very careful in the words that I used and I stick by those words, and my learned friend's attempt to have us agree to something which is quite, quite different, we refuse to be drawn into that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What happened, as matter of fact, there seemed to be an agreement, although limited, on the theoretical level, the abstract level, whereas Ms. Marcus wants to explore what that means on the concrete level and that's where the parties quickly and strongly take their own routes, and I think we should leave it to that, if the parties would agree with my brief analysis of what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I certainly do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I fully agree. I think Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed as you deem fit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, do you recall the date when Operation Pauk ended?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the date when Krajina fell, in practical terms. It was either on the 9th or 10th of August, I believe, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Isn't it a fact as well that Tactical Groups 2 and 3 under Legija and Bozovic were operating in the context of Operation Pauk in the Velika Kladusa area then throughout May, June, July, and into August, as you say, until the Krajina fell?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tactical Groups 2 and 3 functioned during that period of time. However, I don't know whether Bozovic and Legija stayed until the very end. I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, I'd like to clarify to you what our position is with respect to Operation Pauk before I move on to a different subject. Our position is that the accused Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic in their capacity within the Serbian DB directed, financed, equipped, and otherwise supported groups who participated in the Pauk Joint Command. Among the groups supported by the accused and the Serbian DB in their operations in Velika Kladusa were special units of the Serbian MUP under Bozovic, Arkan's SDG, and the Skorpions under Slobodan Medic, aka Boca. We do not dispute that as part of his direct participation in Operation Pauk Franko Simatovic may have been gathering intelligence; that would be logical in his position in the Serbian DB. However, our position is that Mr. Simatovic was also directly involved in day-to-day operations in connection with this Joint Command. The Pauk Joint Command was just, in our position, one example of both accused directing, financing, equipping, training, and otherwise supporting special units of the Serbian DB who then acted in collaboration and co-ordination with other Serb forces throughout the war in both Croatia and Bosnia. Would you like to provide any comment on that position?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Our position with respect to your evidence regarding the Serbia -- Serbian DB's participation in Pauk, and in particular Franko Simatovic's participation in Operation Pauk, is that either you were genuinely not aware of the scope of Mr. Simatovic's and the Serbian DB's activities, or you have not been entirely forthcoming with us about what you do know. Would you like to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I want to be entirely forthcoming, indeed. I have nothing to hide. I was not aware of all these things you just enumerated. I don't know if I'm to blame for that. I know what Franko Simatovic was doing, but whether he was doing anything else, I don't know. In fact, I didn't know until I came here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, could we try to get matters clear. You say, in fact, I didn't know until I came here. Well, you still do not know, although you have seen some documents which may, I'm cautious in saying, may shed light on what has happened and what was being to your knowledge. Do I understand that what was put to you as the Prosecution's case, which is not necessarily the truth, that you have no knowledge about what Ms. Marcus told you, what goes beyond your own personal knowledge of Mr. Simatovic's activities and that because you don't know you can't tell us whether it's true or not true, and that you have been candid as far as your own knowledge is concerned, and what is beyond your knowledge, you cannot comment on. Is that -- is that your position? Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if you say, I didn't know until I came here, you still do not know. The only thing you now know is you have seen a few documents which may suggest that you had no full knowledge of what may have happened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've said looking at the documents that were shown me here that they could be read to mean that they assisted in certain combat activities with their involvement at Petrova Gora.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You still cannot confirm, because of lack of personal knowledge, whether what these documents suggest is true or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no personal knowledge, no other personal knowledge. I can only comment on the document before me. My personal knowledge did not go that far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could I please have Exhibit P468, page 15 in both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: During your testimony, Mr. Bakrac showed you this page from this exhibit. You will see it coming up in a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise, this is a confidential exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, yes. Could it then not be broadcast to the public. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: This is a list of name with Mile Mrksic's name at the top, a list of servicemen. When you see it, perhaps you will tell us if you recall having seen this.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see only the front page. I don't see the list of persons. Yes. Now, I see it. I remember this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You identified many names on this list as active-duty servicemen at the time that they were on this list. That's July 1995, and you provided us with their unit and rank. Do you know the individual at number 30, Nenad Bursac?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'll turn to this document in a few minutes to ask you some more questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please call up 65 ter 6411. Your Honours, this is a document that was received by the OTP from the government of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, this appears to be a transcript of a summary of an intercept provided by the Croatian government. The date is 29th of June, 1995. I'll give you a moment to read this and see if you have any factual knowledge to corroborate it. As you can see, it says: "Aside from all this --" now I'm reading from somewhere in the middle: "Aside from all this, a certain Frenki is also mentioned, possibly from KSS special forces corps Yugoslavia, who could resolve this problem for them and through whom everything was, most probably, organised. Also, from the same conversation, we learn that there was a rotation of instructors on the 29th of June, 1995 (the shift consisting of Colonel Bursac Nenad, Warrant Officer 2nd class Borojevic Predrag and Staff Sergeant Milosavljevic Milisav), and they went to the rotation in a vehicle with a trailer carrying their equipment. It is not known what kind of instructors they are or where they went for the shift rotation ..." You said you didn't know Nenad Bursac. Do you know either Predrag Borojevic or Milisav Milosavljevic who are mentioned in this summary?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know either of the three.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were you aware of a rotation of instructors that took place on the 29th of June, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Then I'll leave this document. Could I now please have 65 ter 6412. And also this should not be broadcast to the public, please. It was received from the Serbian government in response to RFA 1851. Mr. Karan, could I ask you to have a look at this document. I will read the first paragraph and then I'll ask you to read the rest of the document. It's not that long. Maybe you could let us know when you're finished the page so that we can move on to the next one. This is a military secret report on assignment -- on an assignment called Splav, and it states at the beginning: "On the 24th of June, 1995, after the preparation of troops and materiel and technical equipment, they were placed and stored accordingly. The material equipment was stored and secured by a Serbian MUP unit in the castle 'Tikves,' and the troops were accommodated in Bilja, in the facilities of the Serbian MUP. The arrival and accommodation of both troops and equipment was executed in full secrecy. In the following period, until the beginning of the activities, reconnaissance of supply and infiltration routes, in co-operation with the 63rd Parachute Brigade, the 37th Infantry Brigade BOS, combat security, and Serbian MUP units has been carried out." Could I ask you to read further and let us know when you need the page turned.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could we perhaps also move to the second page while the witness is on the B/C/S page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can turn the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: As you can see here on page 3 in English and page 2 in B/C/S, it says: "The entire action was prepared and conducted professionally and skillfully, combining the efforts of both troops and specialist organs." A bit further down it states: "In the course of the execution of the assignment, one MUP Serbia member has been seriously and another slightly wounded, as well as the commander of the group which was working at the water." Isn't it a fact that this report is another example of joint combat operations carried out by a combination of Serbian MUP and active military servicemen?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Objection to the question. Isn't it a fact that the document says X, Y, and Z? In our submission that's what the question amounts to. It's not seeking facts from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry. I believe that it will be very clear what my point is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your point is perfectly clear. Your point is perfectly clear. The question is whether you can put it to the witness in this way. What you apparently are asking the witness is the following: I show you a document which gives facts of which you apparently are unaware. For the Prosecution, these facts indicate that, and then you put what your conclusions are on the basis. Do you have any comment on that? I think that's, Mr. Jordash -- because whether this demonstrates or not would -- first of all, would require that the witness forms an opinion about whether this is an adequate report, whether it's a forgery, whether -- whatever. Of course, the witness cannot know. You say the Prosecution concludes from this document that this and this and this happened, which apparently is not within your knowledge. Can you comment on any of it? Mr. Jordash, would that resolve your --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, is that a question which would provide you with an answer? You -- the only thing you're missing is that the witness agrees this should be the conclusion from this document, or perhaps he does agree, I do not know, but let's ask him this way, what's his knowledge about it. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, do you have any knowledge about this joint operation described in this document, assignment Splav?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This operation was executed in Eastern Slavonija, and at that time I was still with the 21st Corps. I don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You can see that the document was signed by Nenad Bursac. Our position is that Nenad Bursac received payment from the Serbian DB for services he provided in the context of joint Serbian DB military operations. Would you like to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see in this document that he's chief in the special forces corps. He got appointed by the army and he certainly is receiving his salary from the army. I don't see why he would be on the payroll of the state security sector. If he was in the field and from this document we see that he went on field missions, he could have received per diem only from the unit that sent him and that's the special forces corps of the Army of Yugoslavia. That's the only comment I can give because I have no choice. It's an authentic document I'm looking at. I know that from the rectangular stamp, and that's -- there's nothing else I can say about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I please have P468, page 15, again, not to be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You've said you don't know see why Nenad Bursac would be on the payroll of the state security sector. You see that he is here among some other military members. Our position is that some military members like Nenad Bursac received payments by the Serbian DB for services performed at the Serbian DB's bidding, and that explains why they're on this payment list. Would you like to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness is receiving interpretation they were receiving salaries. I think it should be made clear to the witness that we're actually discussing per diems so he can answer appropriately.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the word I chose to use was payments which is neutral in English. Perhaps in English it doesn't specify what type of payment whether it be a salary or a per diem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please again put the question to the witness. Everyone is now fully aware of why you have chosen the words you are using.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Our position, Mr. Karan, is that some military members like Nenad Bursac received a payment by the Serbian DB for services performed at the Serbian DB's bidding and that explains why they are on this payment list. I ask if you'd like to comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the list, but I don't see what financial authority's providing these payments. I can see it's a list of persons receiving per diem, but I cannot conclude from this where the funds came from. I can only see that they received payments in a certain period, and I know some people among the names on the list, but I can't see the source from which payments were made so that they would be doing this work in a certain period. It's an unusual document in some way.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'll show you the first page of this document. It's a 21-page document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please turn to page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And meanwhile I'll ask you a few additional questions. When Mr. Bakrac showed you this list he asked if you knew these people to be members of the JATD of the Serbian DB. So is it your evidence then that you were not aware of payments being issued by the Serbian DB to military servicemen whose names appeared on page 15 of this document?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know of any such thing. I only recognised persons from a list shown to me because I'm friends with many of them, I know them, and those people I identified.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a few other pages from this same document and tell you what our position is on that and give you an opportunity to tell us your comments on that. Could I please have page 4. As you see, Radojica Bozovic is at the top of this list. Our case is that Bozovic was a central member and in fact leader of a special unit of the Serbian DB and that he was paid by the Serbian DB in July 1995, on this list, due to his continued operations in Pauk as commander of Tactical Group 3. I would note for your information that Bozovic appears on 58 payment records, at least, from the Serbian DB from mid-1993 to the end of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I please have page 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you know Vasilije Mijovic and Zivojin Ivanovic or either of them?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: As you can see, these individuals were also paid by the Serbian DB. I note for the record that Mijovic appears on 47 payment lists between 1993 and 1995, and Zika Ivanovic, aka Crnogorac, appears on six payment lists between December 1994 and July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I please have page 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Here you see Milorad Ulemek, aka Legija, whom we discussed earlier. Our position is that others on this list are also members of Arkan's SDG. As you can see the Serbian DB paid Arkan's men for their assistance in combat operations in Operation Pauk, and their appearance on payment records through the rest of 1995, we say, is consistent with their participation in joint combat operations with other Serb forces under the direction and support of the Serbian DB.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I please have page 13. I will give you a chance to make your comments after.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution kindly slow down while reading. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I will do my very best.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, our position is that those on this list are family members of individuals who died in the context of Serbian DB operations, some of whom died as early as 1992. For example, Branko Dimic at number 2, his son, Milan, died in combat operations in Doboj on the 13th of July, 1992. That is our position. And that Branko Dimic, his father, was paid by the Serbian DB for his son's services in furtherance of the DB operations in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Finally, could I please have page 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, auction see here Janko Keres is at number 8. He was the author of the JATD report for the Pauk operation that we looked at a short while ago and he's on this payment list. By the time he wrote the report which we looked at and certainly by the time he was paid on this list, July 1995, he was indeed a member of the JATD. That is our case. However, our position is that he was operating as a member of the special units of the Serbian DB since 1993. Isn't it a fact that you were simply not aware of the degree of involvement of the Serbian DB in participating in and supporting joint combat operations in the areas in which you served as a security operative or, indeed, in other regions?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of those activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I would like to note for the record that what my learned friend has just put to the witness concerning the family members, son Milan who died in combat operations in Doboj, Branko Dimic, the father being paid by the Serbian DB for his son's services in Doboj, and the allegations concerning Janko Keres are the very first time we've heard allegations, I think, in this case. For three years into this case the Prosecution are now specifying what their case is in relation to these payment lists, and this is a problem I flagged up several years ago, that producing payment lists without any indication of what those individuals have said to have done, who they were, what their acts and conduct were, how it contributed to the crime and how they are linked to the accused was always going to be a problem, a big problem about notice. It's impossible -- sorry, it's not impossible, but now it's highly impracticable for the Defence to deal with these allegations now specified. If they'd been identified and dealt with and specified three years ago, we could have cross-examined a huge number of witnesses, we could have called Defence evidence to deal with these allegations, but as it is, at the dawn of the closing of the case, we are now understanding what significance the Prosecution intends to place on these individuals. Completely unfair, in our respectful submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour as Mr. Jordash forecasted yesterday, our pleadings have been quite clear about how the payment lists prove our case or support the evidence in our case. They are one part of the evidence. We have included very clear submission on that in 98 bis. Going person by person is detail all included in our general submissions about how the payment records demonstrate the DB's role. We've shown what contribution we allege the DB to have been involved in. We never said that every single member on these payment lists was a member of the JATD. We never made that submission. We made it quite clear what the payment lists show. Now, I've given detailed examples which are fully consistent with our overall submissions regarding the payment lists. So I'm going to make this quite clear, even clearer to the witness, give him an opportunity to comment on it, and in our submission we've met our obligation clearly in our pleadings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I don't want to detain the witness obviously, but I do invite -- I would like to respond very briefly to what my learned friend has said, which is, in our submission, completely inaccurate. I've been proceeding, maybe it's my fault, but I've been proceeding on the basis that the payment lists are a reflection, according to the Prosecution, of who was in the JATD, and I suspect the Simatovic team have been proceeding on the same basis. Until, of course, now when we have what is effectively a volte-face and the Prosecution now saying, Well, actually, it's not just the JATD, it's something quite different. And in relation to the individuals that have just been mentioned, these are the specifics in relation to them. And the problem is that there are hundreds of people on the payment lists. If we have a misunderstanding about what the Prosecution case is in relation to something as basic as whether the members on the -- those mentioned on the payment list represent the JATD or something else, then we are heading into multiple misunderstandings when it comes to the specifics that the Prosecution now are going to seek to allege. The closing brief is going to be the first time that many of these individuals are identified properly by the Prosecution and a proper description put as to what it is the Prosecution say they did in connection to the accused. Of course we can't deal with that at that stage, but in relation to most of the names, that is the situation it seems that we're now into because of this shift from the idea that the payment lists represent the JATD to now actually they represent something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour. Your Honour, my learned friend Mr. Jordash said that he assumed that our team shared his position, and would I like to state for the record that we share the same position. And that one of the main reasons for that was when we showed per diems to this witness, we were surprised that the per diem lists contained the names of active-duty officers who were still serving in the army, and practically it is only now that we receive information from the Prosecutor about their thesis with regard to the vast number of individuals whose names can be found on those payment lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I just add two sentences, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, two.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In our respectful submission, that's precisely why the Prosecution have shifted their position, because it has become clear to the Prosecution through Defence evidence that people on this payment list were not members of the JATD but were members of other military formations, and the Prosecution's shift is to deal with that evidence whilst purporting to maintain consistency in their case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. First of all, if Mr. Jordash would point to anywhere where we alleged that every name on the payment lists was the name of a member of the JATD, we will certainly consider that to have been in error. I do not believe we have ever said that because that has never been our case. Secondly, Your Honour, and more broadly, there are general pleadings in the case. There is the indictment. There is the pre-trial brief, and we've also at the conclusion of our evidence had 98 bis. We don't go through every paragraph of every document and explain every single paragraph. Neither does the Defence. They put forward their general pleadings and then they tender evidence in support of that. The evidence is discussed with witnesses. Witnesses contextualise that evidence. Some of it comes in in bar table motions and not every single line is dealt with. What our position is is that the payment records are another example of documentary evidence. We have clearly said what our position is with respect to what the payment lists show in terms of the accusations against the accused. These examples support that position and are merely that, example of how the payment records fit in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- Mr. Jordash showed some self-restraint. If you'd do the same at this moment, Ms. Marcus. I do understand. What keeps the parties at this moment apart is that the Defence says, We were under the impression, an impression given by the Prosecution, that persons which appear on the payment list were JATD members and it's only now at a later stage that we learn from the Prosecution that their actual position is that those the Prosecution claims were members of the JATD appear on these lists but possibly together with others who were not members of the JATD.
